newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt to investigate claimed Oppn abuses.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt to investigate claimed Oppn abuses.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it would investigate claims that the former Labor government allowed labour union members to use electoral offices for their own purposes.
The government said claims had been made that two Labor government ministers had handed over their Melbourne offices to the Transport Workers' Union for up to eight months.
Govermment leader in the lower house of parliament Peter Reith said taxpayer resources had been grossly misused if the claims proved to be correct.
Reith said he would ask Administrative Services Minister David Jull to confirm whether this occupation took place and for how long.

"I will also ask Mr Jull to examine the phone records of the period involved to determine whether any funds can be recovered from the union and whether any rent can be levied for the use of prime office space in Melbourne," Reith said in a statement.
The claims involved the former offices of current opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans and former Defence Minister Robert Ray.
Support for the conservative Liberal-National coalition, which came into power in March 1996 after 13 years of Labor government, has dropped sharply during a two-month scandal over expense abuses.
Last Friday, Australian Prime Minister John Howard pledged to stamp out parliamentary corruption.
